title: Carbon monoxide after the power goes out

sources.name: CDC — About Carbon Monoxide (CO) Poisoning Prevention
U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission — Carbon Monoxide Information Center
American Red Cross — Power Outage Safety
sources.note: not verified here — the fetch was refused

quotes.cdc_generator_indoor: Never use a generator inside your home or garage, even if doors and windows are open.
quotes.cdc_distance: Only use generators outside, more than 20 feet away from any windows, doors, and vents.
quotes.cpsc_distance: Never use portable generators inside homes or garages, even if doors and windows are open. Use generators outside only, at least 20 feet away from homes with exhaust facing away.
quotes.ready_distance: Generators and fuel should always be used outdoors and at least 20 feet away from windows, doors and attached garages.
quotes.ready_stove: Generators, camp stoves or charcoal grills should always be used outdoors and at least 20 feet away from windows.
quotes.cdc_charcoal: Never burn charcoal indoors. Burning charcoal - red, gray, black, or white - gives off CO.
quotes.cdc_camp_stove: Never use a portable gas camp stove indoors.
quotes.cdc_gas_oven_heat: Never heat your house with a gas oven.
quotes.ready_gas_oven_heat: Do not use a gas stove or oven to heat your home. It increases your risk of carbon monoxide poisoning.
quotes.cdc_deaths: Each year, more than 400 Americans die from unintentional CO poisoning not linked to fires, more than 100,000 visit an emergency department, and more than 14,000 are hospitalized.
quotes.cpsc_deaths: More than 200 people in the United States die every year from accidental non-fire related CO poisoning associated with consumer products. More than 100 of those deaths are linked to portable generators.
quotes.cdc_symptoms: The most common symptoms of CO poisoning are headache, dizziness, weakness, upset stomach, vomiting, chest pain, and confusion. CO symptoms are often described as “flu-like.”
quotes.cpsc_symptoms_action: Know the symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning: headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea, vomiting, sleepiness, and confusion. If you suspect CO poisoning, get outside to fresh air immediately, and then call 911.
quotes.cdc_alarm_replace: Replace your CO detector following the manufacturer's instructions or every 5 years.
quotes.cdc_alarm_place: Install battery-operated or battery back-up CO detectors near every sleeping area in your home.
quotes.cpsc_alarm_place: Install battery-operated CO alarms or CO alarms with battery backup on every level of the home and outside sleeping areas. Interconnected CO alarms are best; when one sounds, they all sound.
quotes.ready_alarm_place: Install carbon monoxide detectors with battery backup in central locations on every level of your home.
quotes.cdc_car_garage: Never run your car or truck inside a garage that is attached to a house, even with the garage door open.

disagreements.what: how many people CO kills each year
disagreements.cdc: more than 400, all unintentional non-fire CO deaths
disagreements.cpsc: more than 200, CO deaths associated with consumer products (more than 100 from portable generators alone)
disagreements.why_it_reads_as_a_contradiction: 200 is not a typo for 400 — the two agencies count different populations. A page that prints one without the other is reporting the choice it made.

disagreements.what: how far from the building a generator must sit
disagreements.cdc: more than 20 feet from windows, doors, and vents
disagreements.cpsc: at least 20 feet from homes, with exhaust facing away
disagreements.ready: at least 20 feet from windows, doors and attached garages
disagreements.why_it_reads_as_a_contradiction: all three land on 20 feet but differ on 20 feet from what, and only CPSC names the direction the exhaust must face.

disagreements.cdc: headache, dizziness, weakness, upset stomach, vomiting, chest pain, and confusion
disagreements.cpsc: headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea, vomiting, sleepiness, and confusion
disagreements.why_it_reads_as_a_contradiction: the lists are close but not identical; a symptom one body names and the other does not is still a reason to leave the room.

disagreements.what: when to replace a CO alarm
disagreements.cdc: following the manufacturer's instructions or every 5 years
disagreements.cpsc: no interval given (placement and interconnection only)
disagreements.why_it_reads_as_a_contradiction: only one of the three gives a number; the page prints the 5-year figure as the CDC's and says the manufacturer's label wins.
